promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: the real bridge, camera and room; repaint, never move
Image 2: Identity only: Castle's face, hair and jacket; not layout or style

Use case: sketch-to-render. One landscape 3:2 (1536x1024) cinematic story illustration for a mature industrial science-fiction game. Restrained realistic hand-painted finish, charcoal steel, dirty amber work lights, muted blue shadows, tactile worn metal, believable human scale. Readable when reduced to 1200x800. No legible text, no logos, watermarks, border, interface, ornate armor or luxury.

Scene: late on the Second Wind's bridge. Castle, the company's operations officer, writes a message to an old friend she has not spoken to in years, while patrols crawl across the navigation display.

Reference 1 is a render of the real bridge and is the authority for the room: keep its camera, perspective, the port comms bank (the long console of grey-green cabinets with three screens, two small amber indicator lamps and a row of coloured lamps), the round plot table edge in the lower left, the ceiling pipes and caged strip lamp, the wall cabinets on the left and the narrow slit windows above the bank. Do not enlarge the windows. Paint it as the same worn grey-green room, scuffed and lived in, lit mostly by the screens and one ceiling lamp.

Castle, exactly the woman in Reference 2 (her face, age, greying dark hair in a short practical bun, charcoal-olive high-collared duty jacket, small earpiece with boom mic), stands at the comms bank a little left of centre, leaning on it with one forearm and typing slowly with the other hand. Seen three-quarter from behind her right shoulder so her face shows in profile, lit green-white by the screens. She is careful and a little uncertain, reading what she has written before sending. Medium size in frame, the console around her.

The centre screen shows a dark navigation plot with a few small amber patrol markers and their dotted tracks; the right screen shows a message thread as blurred unreadable lines. Nothing readable. Through the slit windows: dark space with the scattered lights of distant freighters and stations.

Nobody else. Quiet, private, a little lonely.
